A competitive market has demand Qd = 100 − P and supply Qs = 20 + 3P (P in dollars). The government imposes a per-unit tax of $8.

What is the quantity traded after the tax is imposed? Reply with only that number and no other figures.
items.reasoning: We need quantity after tax. Demand Qd = 100 - P. Supply Qs = 20 + 3P. But with per-unit tax of $8, the supply curve shifts upward: suppliers receive price net of tax? Usually with a tax on sellers, suppliers receive P - t, but demand sees price P. So supply equation becomes Qs = 20 + 3(P - t) or equivalently Qs = 20 + 3P - 3t. t=8 => Qs = 20 + 3P - 24 = -4 + 3P. Wait 20-24 = -4. So Qs = -4 + 3P. Set equal to demand: 100 - P = -4 + 3P. Solve: 100 + 4 = 3P + P => 104 = 4P => P = 26. Then Q = 100 - 26 = 74. Alternatively Qs: -4 + 3*26 = -4 + 78 = 74. So quantity traded after tax is 74. Provide only that number.

Demand: Qd = 100 - P.
